decision.summary: The Fed raised its policy rate by 25 basis points, to 5.25% to 5.5%. The vote was 11-0.

changes.quote: Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has been expanding at a moderate pace.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has continued to expand at a modest pace.”

changes.quote: In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “In support of these goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 5 to 5-1/4 percent.”

changes.quote: The Committee will continue to assess additional information and its implications for monetary policy.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Holding the target range steady at this meeting allows the Committee to assess additional information and its implications for monetary policy.”

tone_quotes.quote: In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent.

In determining the extent of additional policy firming that may be appropriate to return inflation to 2 percent over time, the Committee will take into account the cumulative tightening of monetary policy, the lags with which monetary policy affects economic activity and inflation, and economic and financial developments.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 20.09% APR, a 25 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3.86% and moved -5 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.96% would fall by about $10.05 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 3.6%, and employers added an average of 249k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 3.1% over the past year (June 2023); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 4.4%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -3 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0.02%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.08% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is hawkish (leaning toward higher rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 49%, cut 2%, hike 49%.
